prompt_source.definition: alpha is the total deflection angle, i.e. the angle between incoming and outgoing asymptotic velocity directions

provided_solution_record.scope: The provided solution presents this single final formula for the combined parts B2(c)(i)-(ii).
provided_solution_record.derivation_summary: It sets alpha=2 arccos(1/e), uses B=r0/sqrt(e^2-1), and concludes B(alpha)=r0 cot(alpha/2).
provided_solution_record.retention_policy: Retain unchanged as provided-solution evidence; do not silently replace it with the adjudicated reference.

issues: The printed derivation uses the angle between position-ray asymptotes, 2 arccos(1/e), rather than the prompt-defined angle between incoming and outgoing velocity directions.
The printed final result treats the orbit-dependent semilatus rectum r0 as if it were constant across the fixed-energy impact-parameter family.

adjudicated_reference.part_c_i: B(alpha_s)=a_C cot(alpha_s/2), where a_C=k q_alpha q_gamma/(m_gamma v_inf^2).
adjudicated_reference.part_c_ii: For the part-(b) reference trajectory e=3 and p=r0, so a_C=r0/(e^2-1)=r0/8 and B(alpha_s)=(r0/8) cot(alpha_s/2).
adjudicated_reference.notation: alpha_s denotes the prompt-defined physical velocity deflection and distinguishes it from the supplementary angle used in the source solution.

derivation: For repulsive Coulomb scattering at fixed asymptotic speed, define a_C=k q_alpha q_gamma/(m_gamma v_inf^2).
Conservation of energy and angular momentum gives e^2=1+(B/a_C)^2.
For r=p/(e cos(phi)-1), the position-ray asymptote has phi_inf=arccos(1/e), while the incoming velocity points opposite the incoming position ray.
Therefore the physical velocity deflection is alpha_s=pi-2 phi_inf=2 arcsin(1/e), which yields B=a_C cot(alpha_s/2).
The semilatus rectum obeys p=a_C(e^2-1). For the part-(b) reference trajectory, e=3 and p=r0=4 m, hence a_C=r0/8.
